title: Push verified candidate early to PR branch when verification starts
summary: When verification of a job starts, athena land pushes the verified candidate to the job's PR branch through the host seam (Remote::push in gh.rs), so CI's 'fmt, clippy, tests' runs and caches during verification. A push failure is logged and ignored; the landing still pushes the landing commit to the same branch. The audience is the maintainer who wants faster landings.

defaults_applied.how: Tests with fake host; cargo test and clippy clean.
Criteria check push calls and unchanged outcome on failure.
One focused change in gh.rs and run.rs.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The existing Remote::push(branch, commit) seam in gh.rs is reused; no workflow file change is needed since part 1 already caches by fingerprint.
The early push happens in run.rs at the start of the verification phase, with the branch name the landing uses.
A push failure is logged and swallowed; no new record type is required.
The early-pushed candidate is the code whose governed fingerprint matches what landing will push, so CI cache reuse works.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test using the fake host/remote records an early push of the candidate commit to the job's PR branch when verification starts, before verification completes. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
A test shows that when the early push returns an error, the job's outcome is identical to the no-push-failure case (no job failure, landing proceeds as today). Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
A test shows landing still pushes the job's landing commit to the same branch after the early push. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
cargo test and cargo clippy pass with no warnings, and cargo fmt --check is clean.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the early push to the PR branch during verification and that push failures are non-fatal.

out_of_scope: Changing how the landing commit is built or merged
